transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I haven’t really been myself lately. It’s probably nothing dramatic, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve kind of stopped doing the things I used to do—hiking, coaching, playing guitar. I don’t call people back much either.

Some days I’m just in my rental, and I know there are things I should be doing, but I just sit there for hours and can’t seem to get started. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
How long have you been feeling this way—withdrawing from activities and struggling to get started—has it been weeks, months, or longer?

I guess… longer than weeks. It kind of started after I moved into the smaller rental after the divorce. That was about a year and two months ago now.

I don’t know if it was all at once, but that’s when things started sort of… unraveling, I guess. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal, even if it didn't last long?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the way you’re describing, anyway.

I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep great, but I wouldn’t say I felt elated or full of energy for days. If anything, it’s more the opposite. I mean, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean by “unusually energetic”?
Before this period started about 14 months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of feeling down, unmotivated, and withdrawn like this in the past?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I had anything quite like this before… not this long, anyway.

I mean, I’ve had rough patches like anybody—work stress, life stuff—but I was still basically functioning, still doing my usual things. This feels different, I guess. Is that helpful?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, or in how much you're sleeping compared to before?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really been tracking it closely.

Sleep maybe isn’t great, but it’s hard to say if it’s different from before. Appetite… I don’t think there’s been some big change that I’ve noticed. My weight seems about the same, I think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over these past 14 months, have you felt this way—low and unmotivated—nearly every day, or have there been stretches, even a few weeks at a time, where you felt more like your normal self?

It’s been… pretty close to every day, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I don’t really feel like myself anymore.

There might be better days here and there, but not really whole stretches where I’m back to normal. I used to hike, coach, play guitar, call people back… and I just kind of stopped. Some days I’ll sit in my rental for hours knowing there are things I should do, and I just can’t get myself to start.

I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Along with feeling low and unmotivated, have you noticed things like difficulty concentrating, feeling worthless or excessively guilty, or having thoughts about death or that life isn't worth living?

I don’t know… concentration maybe isn’t great, but I’m not sure if that’s what you mean. I can still follow things if I really have to, it just takes more effort sometimes.

As far as feeling worthless or guilty, I wouldn’t say it like that exactly. I get frustrated with myself, sure, because I’m not doing what I used to do, but I don’t want to overstate it.

And thoughts about death… no, I don’t think so. Not in a serious way. I mean, I get tired of things being like this, but I’m not sitting around planning anything or anything like that. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy nearly every day during this time, even when you haven't been physically active?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I do feel worn out sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s nearly every day or unusual.

I haven’t been doing as much, so it’s hard to tell if it’s real tiredness or just… me not getting going. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic if it’s not. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you or people close to you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or conversely feeling physically restless and unable to sit still, during this period?

I don’t think so… not that anyone’s really said to me.

I mean, maybe I’m quieter than I used to be, but I don’t know if I’m actually speaking slower. And I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around or can’t sit still or anything like that. Mostly I just kind of sit there.

Sorry, I’m not sure if that’s helpful.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic depressive syndrome lasting over a year (exceeding the 2-year adult threshold trend but at minimum meeting the 1-year+ criterion), with low mood, anhedonia (loss of interest in hiking, coaching, guitar, socializing), amotivation, and mild concentration difficulty present nearly every day with no significant symptom-free intervals. However, the symptom count and severity fall short of a full Major Depressive Episode: he explicitly denies appetite/weight change, denies psychomotor agitation/retardation observed by others, denies significant guilt/worthlessness, denies suicidal ideation, and is uncertain about fatigue being pervasive. This pattern of chronic, low-grade, sub-threshold depressive symptoms causing functional impairment (withdrawal from valued activities, inability to initiate tasks) without discrete episodic remission or manic/hypomanic history is most consistent with Dysthymia (Persistent Depressive Disorder), F34.1, rather than recurrent MDD or an adjustment disorder, given the chronicity and absence of full MDE criteria at any point described.
